text:
maria: Heads up — noticed a recurring pattern in the cross-region Karpenter test: when we create 80+ GPU pods in parallel in eu-west-1 we see a long tail of Pending due to node creation rate + ENI limits.

aj: Yea saw that. Are the pods waiting for specific instance types (p4d) or just GPUs? Could be AZ-level capacity.

taylor: It's mostly p4d pinned by nodeSelector. When capacity flaps, Karpenter kicks off lots of launches and then we hit trunk ENI quotas in the subnet; AWS throttles and node attach times balloon.

maria: Repro steps: run parallel job launching 5 k8s jobs each with 16 replicas (gpu: p4d), use Karpenter provisioner with constraints below.

maria: ```yaml
apiVersion: karpenter.sh/v1alpha5
kind: Provisioner
metadata:
  name: gpu-provisioner
spec:
  requirements:
  - key: karpenter.sh/capacity-type
    operator: In
    values: [on-demand, spot]
  limits:
    resources:
      cpu: 2000
      nvidia.com/gpu: 200
  consolidation:
    enabled: true
  ttlSecondsUntilExpired: 900
```

kevin: Two angles: throttle Karpenter's max provisioning rate (we don't have a native field) or introduce a pre-flight admission controller to spread pod creation over a short window. Also consider subnet ENI headroom by keeping a small pool of warm nodes per AZ.

aj: Could we leverage nodeTemplate with `startupProbe` to delay scheduling until ENI attached? Or set `PodTopologySpread` to bias across AZs to avoid saturating a single subnet.

taylor: For the chaos-run I'm proposing: 1) run 200 pods pinned to p4d, 2) disable consolidation, 3) measure 95th/99th node attach latency, 4) flip consolidation back and measure scheduling jitter. Also capture cloudwatch ENIThrottling metrics.

maria: Sounds good. Action items:
- @aj to prototype slow-admit webhook to batch creation (owner: aj) -> due EOD tomorrow
- @kevin to add warm-node launch config per AZ (owner: kevin) -> due next Tues
- @taylor to run chaos test and share logs + 99p attach latency (owner: taylor) -> due after warm nodes in place
- Infra-bot: create metric dashboard for `eni_attach_latency` and `karpenter_node_launch_rate`

infra-bot: Created task INFRA-4221 and dashboard stub: https://grafana.internal/redwood/d/eni-throttle

aj: I'll spin up a PoC webhook. Quick Q: do we want the webhook to use a token bucket with burst=5/sec? or sth more conservative.

maria: Start conservative: 2/s per region, with AZ backoff on ENI errors. Keep logs verbose.

kevin: On cost: warm nodes will increase baseline spend — estimate ~+12% for our eu-west-1 GPU fleet but should reduce wasted retries and spot churn. We'll track cost delta in the dashboard.

taylor: I'll post the first run results in this thread when done. If we see ENI remains the bottleneck we may need subnet scaling or multi-subnet assignment.

maria: Thanks everyone. Let's keep updates short in thread. :thumbsup:
